findings.title: errors[] token enumeration incomplete vs actual fetchGradeGames throws
findings.problem: §1.4 claims the errors[].error tokens are exactly 'rate_limited | forbidden | not_found | upstream_error', said to be verbatim from fetchGradeGames. The worker's fetchGradeGames also throws UpstreamError('api_key_not_configured', 500) when env.PHQ_API_KEY is unset, so that token is missing from the set. Cosmetic only: the frontend treats errors[] as opaque and never branches on the token.
findings.fix: Add api_key_not_configured to the enumerated set in §1.4 and the §1.11 row (rate_limited | forbidden | not_found | upstream_error | api_key_not_configured, plus fetch_failed), or soften to 'includes but is not limited to'.

findings.title: stripGrade vs stripGradeName naming mismatch
findings.problem: §1.8 names the team-name helper stripGrade (matching the push pipeline's in-file regex), while §1.9 lists the pure helper to extract as stripGradeName. Two names for one helper could yield two implementations. The real push-pipeline helper also defaults null to '?' ((n ?? '?')), which the design does not reproduce.
findings.fix: Use one name across §1.8 and §1.9 (suggest stripGradeName for the exported pure helper), and either reproduce the '?' fallback or state it is intentionally dropped because the grade-feed competitor name is non-null.

findings.title: clarify the match name source matches the push pipeline, not just the regex
findings.problem: §1.8 says stripGrade is 'the same regex the push pipeline uses' but builds match from the grade-feed competitors[].name, whereas the pipeline strips live.home.name. Verified these resolve from the same grade-feed competitor names (toFixtureLite / teamOf), so the reuse is sound, but the document should state it to avoid a reader worrying the sources differ.
findings.fix: Add one sentence to §1.8 noting the grade-feed competitors[].name is the same field the push pipeline ultimately strips, so the suffix pattern matches.
